title: scorzoneroides pyrenaica subsp. cantabrica
intro: Scorzoneroides pyrenaica subsp. cantabrica, commonly known as the Cantabrian Scorzonera or Pyrenean Scorzonera, is a type of flowering plant in the dandelion family (Asteraceae). It is a perennial plant native to the mountainous regions of northern Spain and southern France, known for its edible roots, which have been used for centuries in traditional medicine for their potential health benefits. The roots of Scorzoneroides pyrenaica subsp. cantabrica are rich in inulin, a prebiotic fiber with health benefits including lowering cholesterol levels, regulating blood sugar, and supporting gut health. The plant's bioactive constituents include sesquiterpene lactones, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which exhibit anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, contributing to its therapeutic actions in treating various health conditions.
